newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. Council tells Albania to stop violence.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Council tells Albania to stop violence.

text.p: The U.N. Security Council late on Thursday appealed to Albanians to stop violence throughout the country as the government moved tanks into the streets to stem a revolt in the Balkan country.

In a statement read at a formal meeting at the request of Albania and Italy, the council urged "all concerned to refrain from hostilities and acts of violence and to cooperate with diplomatic efforts to reach a peaceful solution to the crisis."
"It urges all political forces to work together to lower tension and facilitate the stablization of the country," the council said.

The council, however, made no reference to a call from Albania's beleaguered government for foreign military intervention to halt the chaos as the country drifted towards anarchy. Tanks appeared on the streets of Tirana late on Thursday.

Albania's U.N. ambassador, Pellumb Kulla, said he wanted the council to "make an appeal to our population because the country was out of control and the people through this statement should have a source of optimism for the future."
He told reporters the new Albanian government welcomed such a statement.

Italy's ambassador Paoli Fulci said that "we think a real massacre could start any moment in Albania and we think it is important to assure the people that someone is working on the Albanian problem."
Fulci wanted the statement adopted hours earlier but Chinese envoys said they could not reach their superiors in Beijing until dawn local time, diplomats reported.

More than 40 people have died in violence since January, initially sparked by the collapse of shady pyramid investment schemes, which drew in the savings of hundreds of thousands. Many of the rebels believe some government leaders either benefitted or turned a blind eye to the fraud.
The council, in its statement, asked Albanaians "not to impede the provision of humanitarian assistance" to civilians and said to keep open communications facilities.
It also said countries should help with humanitarian aid and supported diplomatic efforts by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe and the European Union.
Albanian authorities, buoyed by a new all-party government, had appealed unsuccessfully for calm against an unyielding campaign by rebels demanding the resignation of President Sali Berisha.

Fighters in the south have said they would not give up their weapons until Berisha quit. In some areas the rebellion visibly deteriorated into lawlessness with armed gangs roaming through rebel-held towns, robbing motorists, terrorising women and shooting at travelers.
